title: Contracting out that a union objected to, against the classes that could do the work
question: On the Civil Service Commission list of 16 June 2025, which requests to contract out drew a union objection, which City classes and unions did the department name, and how many City employees hold those classes?
finding: 4 of 11 requests drew a union objection, worth $80.2 million. The largest, $30.0 million for unarmed guards at the public hospitals and clinics, named one class, 8300 Sheriff's Cadet, and one union, 790 SEIU, Local 1021, Misc; 94 people held that class in fiscal 2026 (Sheriff 94 rows; none in Public Health), and they were paid $3.3 million of overtime. The same year the Sheriff paid $62.2 million of overtime, 76.9% of it to Deputy Sheriffs' Assoc (DSA) (unit 498), a unit the request does not name.
how: The union-notice page of each request (OCR text of the Commission's item 8) gives the job classes and unions the department notified; the objection flag and amounts are the peer_pay screen's. Holders and overtime are the Controller's fiscal 2026 rows for those job codes, citywide and in the requesting department; each class's unit is the Department of Human Resources' union code for it.
limits: Contracting out is permitted when the Commission approves it; a department picks the classes it notifies, and the notice is not a finding that the class could do the work. Grant terms can require community providers. Whether the Commission approved these requests, and on what terms, is not in the item. The OCR can misread a class number; each was checked against the rate table.
